surveyDefinition.title: Organic Milk — consumer survey (Europe)
surveyDefinition.whatThisSurveyIs: A business-to-consumer (B2C) market research questionnaire about Organic Milk. Every question asks about Organic Milk specifically — not the wider market, not adjacent categories, and not any named brand. It is designed to tell a client what buyers in Europe actually do and want in this category.
surveyDefinition.whoseContextThisIs: Adults in Europe who buy or use Organic Milk for personal or household use. Respondents qualify if they: Primary or shared grocery decision-maker in the household; Purchases organic milk at least once in the past 3 months; Consumes milk or serves it to household members. Excluded: Institutional buyers (restaurants, cafeterias, schools); Dairy farmers or processors; People who never buy milk or dairy alternatives.
surveyDefinition.whyTheseRespondents: Organic milk is a retail grocery product purchased by households for personal consumption, making it a clear B2C market.
respondentBehaviours: Regularly purchases organic or premium food products
Reads nutrition labels and seeks out certifications (USDA Organic, EU Organic)
Willing to pay a premium for perceived health and environmental benefits
Shoppers at supermarkets, natural food stores, and online grocery delivery
whatIsDeliberatelyNotAsked: Age or household income — these define who was recruited, not what is measured, so they appear in the audience definition rather than as questions.
Brand, company or manufacturer names — the survey stays at category level so findings are not tied to one competitor set.
Where the respondent lives — region is chosen when viewing the results, so asking it again would waste a question.
surveyDefinition.howToReadTheNumbers: Percentages are simulated from a persona-weighted panel of 2,500 synthetic respondents built from real market evidence, not from fieldwork. Single-choice, ranking and rating-scale questions sum to 100%. Multi-select questions do not — each option is an independent share of respondents choosing it. The N shown on each question is the display base for that item.

structure.storyline: Questions run in a planned narrative order: broad and easy first, specific and sensitive last.
structure.storylineSummary: The survey opens by establishing the respondent's relationship with organic milk, then moves through their usage occasions, frequency, household roles, and underlying motivations. It then traces the purchase journey from triggers and discovery through channels, cycle, decision drivers, spend, and routine. Next, it explores product expectations from must-haves and quality cues to packaging, claims, trade-offs, and value. Finally, it assesses satisfaction, friction, switching triggers, advocacy, and future intent, ending on a forward-looking note.

targetCustomer.summary: Adult consumers of Organic Milk in Europe — who Primary or shared grocery decision-maker in the household; Purchases organic milk at least once in the past 3 months; Consumes milk or serves it to household members. The consumer audience for organic milk is defined by household grocery shoppers who prioritize health, sustainability, and product quality, and who actively choose organic over conventional milk.
inclusionCriteria: Primary or shared grocery decision-maker in the household
Purchases organic milk at least once in the past 3 months
Consumes milk or serves it to household members
behaviors: Regularly purchases organic or premium food products
Reads nutrition labels and seeks out certifications (USDA Organic, EU Organic)
Willing to pay a premium for perceived health and environmental benefits
Shoppers at supermarkets, natural food stores, and online grocery delivery
exclusions: People who never buy milk or dairy alternatives

contextDemographics.geography: Urban and suburban areas with access to specialty grocery stores

assumptions: Organic milk is assumed to be a retail product, not a bulk ingredient
Consumers are assumed to be in regions where organic milk is widely available
The survey targets the end consumer, not retailers or distributors
targetCustomer.note: Respondents match this target customer. Age, income, and brand/company-name items are NOT asked in the questionnaire; they may appear here only as research context.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, about how many half-gallon (or 2-liter) containers of organic dairy milk did your household use?
questions.insight: Top response: 2–3 containers (35.00%).

questions.question: Who in your household drinks organic dairy milk? Select all that apply.
options: No one in my household drinks it

questions.insight: Top response: Adults (18 and over) (72.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Adults dominate across all personas; children/toddlers from Urban Eco Parents and Budget Family Shoppers; no one from non-users.

questions.question: Who in your household is mainly responsible for deciding which organic dairy milk to buy?
options: I share the decision with someone else

data.label: I share the decision with someone else

questions.insight: Top response: I am (55.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Self-decision high among single-person households and primary shoppers; shared decisions from couples in Urban Eco Parent and Affluent Quality Seeker segments.

questions.question: How important are each of the following reasons for choosing organic dairy milk over conventional milk?
questions.insight: Top response: Health benefits and nutrition (38.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Health benefits top for Health-Conscious Singles and Urban Eco Parents; sustainability for Eco Activists and Value-Conscious Environmentalists; lactose-free from Lactose-Intolerant Alternative Seekers.

questions.question: Which of the following most often prompts you to buy organic dairy milk?
options: We run out of it at home
It's part of my regular weekly grocery shop
I see it on special offer or discount
A specific meal or recipe calls for it
I buy it when I'm already in the store for other items

data.label: We run out of it at home
It's part of my regular weekly grocery shop
I see it on special offer or discount
A specific meal or recipe calls for it
I buy it when I'm already in the store for other items

questions.insight: Top response: It's part of my regular weekly grocery shop (42.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Regular weekly shopping driven by Urban Eco Parent, Affluent Quality Seeker, Traditional Premium Buyer; special offers pulled by Budget Family Shopper and Value-Conscious Environmentalist.

questions.question: Before buying a new type of organic dairy milk, where do you typically look for information about it?
options: I don't look for information; I just pick one

data.label: I don't look for information; I just pick one

questions.insight: Top response: In-store labels and packaging (35.00%).
questions.distributionNote: In-store labels dominate due to high in-store purchase behavior; online reviews from Digital Native Urbanite and Health-Conscious Single; social media from Eco Activist and Digital Native.

questions.question: How often do you typically buy organic dairy milk?
questions.insight: Top response: About once a week (45.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Weekly purchasing is common across families and health-focused personas; less frequent from singles and lactose-intolerant due to smaller consumption.

questions.question: When you are standing in the dairy aisle, how much do the following factors influence your decision to buy organic dairy milk?
questions.insight: Top response: Certified organic label (e.g., EU Organic) (30.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Price and organic label are top factors; freshness important for Convenience Seeker and Health-Conscious Single; packaging and origin driven by Eco Activist and Urban Eco Parent.

questions.question: Approximately how much does your household spend on organic dairy milk in a typical month?
questions.insight: Top response: €10 to €19 (35.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Middle spending bands reflect medium income; higher spend from Affluent Quality Seeker and Urban Eco Parent; lower from singles and budget-conscious.

I usually buy the same type but occasionally switch
I compare options each time I buy
I buy whatever is on offer or available

I usually buy the same type but occasionally switch
I compare options each time I buy
I buy whatever is on offer or available

questions.insight: Top response: I usually buy the same type but occasionally switch (40.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Habitual buying from Traditional Premium and Affluent; occasional switching from most; comparison from Health-Conscious and Gourmet; offer-driven from Budget and Value-Conscious.

questions.question: How likely are you to switch to a different organic dairy milk if your usual choice is unavailable?
options: Very likely — I'd pick any other organic option
Somewhat likely — I'd pick a different brand but same type
Not very likely — I'd wait until my usual choice is back in stock
Not at all likely — I'd buy conventional milk instead

Somewhat likely — I'd pick a different brand but same type
Not very likely — I'd wait until my usual choice is back in stock

questions.insight: Top response: Somewhat likely — I'd pick a different brand but same type (40.00%).

questions.question: When buying organic dairy milk, which of the following attributes are non-negotiable for you? Select all that apply.
options: Carries a certified organic label (e.g., EU Organic, Bio)
Produced without antibiotics or added hormones

data.label: Carries a certified organic label (e.g., EU Organic, Bio)
Produced without antibiotics or added hormones
Long enough shelf life to avoid waste

questions.insight: Top response: Carries a certified organic label (e.g., EU Organic, Bio) (82.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Organic certification and no-antibiotics are near-universal across personas; pasture-raised driven by Eco Activist, Urban Eco Parent, and Gourmet Foodie; shelf life driven by Health-Conscious Single and Convenience Seeker.

questions.question: How important is a rich, creamy taste when you judge the quality of organic dairy milk?
questions.insight: Top response: Very important (36.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Creamy taste is important to Affluent Quality Seeker, Gourmet Foodie, and Traditional Premium Buyer; Budget Family and Eco Activist are less focused on texture, pulling toward moderate ratings.

questions.question: Which visual or sensory cue most strongly signals freshness to you when buying organic dairy milk?
options: Sell-by date far in the future

data.label: Sell-by date far in the future

questions.insight: Top response: Thick, creamy consistency (28.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Creamy consistency signals quality to Affluent and Gourmet; sell-by date important to Convenience Seeker and Health-Conscious Single; high fat content favored by Traditional Premium Buyer and Gourmet.

questions.question: Which packaging format do you prefer for organic dairy milk?
questions.insight: Top response: Carton (Tetra Pak or similar) (35.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Carton preferred by Eco Activist and Value-Conscious Environmentalist for lower weight/eco credentials; glass favored by Traditional Premium Buyer and Gourmet; plastic chosen by Budget Family and Convenience Seeker for practicality.

questions.question: Which of the following claims or certifications would most increase your trust in an organic dairy milk product? Select all that apply.
options: USDA Organic or EU Organic certification

questions.insight: Top response: USDA Organic or EU Organic certification (78.00%).
questions.distributionNote: EU Organic is baseline trust for all; grass-fed and animal welfare driven by Eco Activist and Urban Eco Parent; local origin important to Traditional Premium Buyer and Eco Activist; carbon-neutral resonates with Eco Activist and Value-Conscious Environmentalist.

questions.question: If you had to choose between a locally sourced organic milk in plastic packaging and a non-local organic milk in glass packaging at the same price, which would you choose?

questions.insight: Top response: Local origin in plastic packaging (42.00%).

questions.question: Compared to conventional dairy milk, how much more would you be willing to pay for organic dairy milk?

questions.insight: Top response: 11–25% more (38.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Budget Family and Value-Conscious Environmentalist cap at 10%; most personas accept 11-25%; Affluent Quality Seeker and Gourmet Foodie willing to pay 26-50%+; Skeptical Convert and Budget Family anchor the 'not pay more' segment.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied are you with the organic dairy milk you currently buy?
questions.insight: Top response: Somewhat satisfied (38.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Health-focused and premium personas (Affluent Quality Seeker, Gourmet Foodie, Urban Eco Parent) skew satisfied; budget and skeptical personas (Budget Family Shopper, Skeptical Convert) add mid/low tail.

metadata.storyline_summary: The survey opens by establishing the respondent's relationship with organic milk, then moves through their usage occasions, frequency, household roles, and underlying motivations. It then traces the purchase journey from triggers and discovery through channels, cycle, decision drivers, spend, and routine. Next, it explores product expectations from must-haves and quality cues to packaging, claims, trade-offs, and value. Finally, it assesses satisfaction, friction, switching triggers, advocacy, and future intent, ending on a forward-looking note.
storyline_notes: For consumer_profile, kept the canonical arc largely intact but emphasized usage occasions and frequency to reflect milk's perishable, consumable nature; no need for replacement/upgrade beats.

For buying_behavior, added a distinct 'discovery' beat early to capture how European shoppers learn about organic milk options, including online and in-store, given the growing market and digital adoption. Placed 'spend' after 'decision_dri

For preferences_expectations, included 'format_packaging' to address lactose-free and UHT variants, which are relevant to European consumers and the lactose-intolerant persona. Also emphasized 'claims_credentials' due to high environmental

For satisfaction_future_intent, followed the canonical order but placed 'advocacy' before 'future_use' to end on a forward-looking, less sensitive note. 'Switching' is kept late as it involves hypothetical behavior change.
No beats were dropped; all canonical beats were used where applicable, with no duplicate canonical mappings.
metadata.classification_reason: Organic milk is a retail grocery product purchased by households for personal consumption, making it a clear B2C market.
